    "date: 2024-11-14; merchant_id: 137",

    "merchant_age_days: 170; cum_orders: 661"
  ],
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "kind": "bustout",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "The dispute-rate breach warrants investigation, but negative volume_z does not support the described sales ramp. New-buyer GMV share does not establish thin buyer accounts, and fulfillment failure is unverified."
    },
    {
      "kind": "marketing_push",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "A campaign could explain some new-buyer activity, but no campaign evidence is supplied and the volume metric does not indicate a spike. Campaign dates and attributed orders would test this benign explanation."
    },
    {
      "kind": "data_issue",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "Incomplete order ingestion or duplicate dispute records could distort the rate, but no pipeline failure is observed. Reconciliation against source records would confirm or dismiss this explanation."
    }
  ],
  "recommended_action": "monitor",
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "Inspect the three dispute records: verify uniqueness, order linkage, reason codes and status; reconcile the 105-order denominator and ingestion completeness.",
    "Check tracking, delivery confirmation and customer correspondence for disputed orders, then a small sample of recent orders. Repeated verified non-delivery would support escalation; documented fulfillment would weaken bust-out.",
    "Reconcile refund requests, approvals and processor records. Zero recorded refunds does not establish that no customers requested refunds.",
    "Review campaign dates, offers and attributed orders; check buyer account history and concentration to distinguish ordinary acquisition from coordinated thin-account purchases."
  ],
  "memo_markdown": "Merchant 137 triggered AUP-06.1 on November 14: three disputes across 105 trailing-30-day orders, with cb_rate_30d of 0.02857142857142857. Recorded GMV was 999752 cents, volume_z was -1.67351278716791, and new_gmv_share was 0.2760674647312534. No refunds were recorded.\n\nThe breach is observed; bust-out is a hypothesis. Current metrics do not show the described sales ramp or establish thin buyer accounts. Zero refunds does not prove successful fulfillment.\n\nRecommend monitor for the next window, with immediate review of the three disputes, delivery evidence, refund requests and source-data completeness. Verified non-delivery combined with coordinated buyer activity would strengthen bust-out and support a reserve or reversible settlement pause. Valid deliveries and resolved dispute explanations would weaken it. Corrected duplicate disputes or missing denominator orders could dismiss the measured breach; a campaign alone would not explain away fulfillment complaints.\n\nReview campaign records and buyer histories. A human owns any payout restriction; offboarding lacks corroborated support."
}
